properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 14 at 10:01PM AKST until November 16 at 7:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations
between 3 and 7 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze.

* WHERE...NW Kenai Peninsula.

* WHEN...From 3 AM Sunday to 7 AM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Monday morning commute. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
Heavy wet snow and ice accumulations could lead to power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop by early Sunday morning and
continue into early Monday morning. Warmer air will work in aloft
by late Sunday night resulting in areas of mixed snow and freezing
rain. There is still some uncertainty as to where the band of
heaviest snow will develop with this system. If this band remains
over the Kenai and Soldotna area for an extended period of time,
snow amounts could be higher.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 14 at 10:01PM AKST until November 15 at 5:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations
between 1 and 4 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze.
Lowest amounts near Chugiak, highest amounts South Anchorage and
the Anchorage Hillside.

* WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations).

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. The
combination of snow and light ice accumulations may result in a few
localized power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow amounts have trended lower as the
steadier snow looks to remain over the Kenai Peninsula. The most
likely scenario is for 1 to 4 inches across the Anchorage Bowl
through Sunday night. There will be a 30 to 40% chance of a brief
period of light freezing rain at the end of the event.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 14 at 10:01PM AKST until November 15 at 10:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations
between 6 and 12 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze.

* WHERE...East Turnagain Arm, including Portage Valley and Girdwood.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM AKST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
Heavy wet snow and ice accumulations could lead to power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop this evening and become
heavy at times through Sunday. By Sunday evening, the snow will
change to rain as an easterly Turnagain Arm wind develops and
temperatures quickly rise into the upper 30s. Snow and pockets of
freezing rain may linger slight longer for Girdwood before
temperatures warm above freezing.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 14 at 10:01PM AKST until November 15 at 11:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations
between 6 and 12 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze
to a few hundredths of an inch.

* WHERE...Interior Kenai Peninsula, Skilak Lake, and Turnagain Pass.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Monday morning commute. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
Heavy wet snow and ice accumulations could lead to power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop across the interior Kenai
Peninsula by late this evening. Snow will continue through Sunday
evening before warmer air begins to move over the region. Snow will
likely change to rain. However, pockets of freezing rain are
possible in typically colder areas along the Seward Highway from
Turnagain Pass to Primrose.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 14 at 10:01PM AKST until November 16 at 10:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations
between 4 and 10 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze.

* WHERE...SW Kenai Peninsula and Southern Kachemak Bay.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Sunday to 10 AM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Monday morning commute. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
Heavy wet snow and ice accumulations could lead to power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow amounts have trended higher as the steady
snow looks to remain over the southern Kenai Peninsula. The most
likely scenario is for 4 to 8 inches of snow along the Sterling
Highway. There is a 40 to 50% chance for snow amounts up to 10
inches for the Homer Bluffs. There is also a 30 to 40% chance for
the snow to end as a brief period of light freezing rain along the
Sterling Highway corridor near Ninilchik and Anchor Point.

change to rain as winds switch to the east and temperatures quickly
rise into the upper 30s. The gusty winds may result in localized
areas of drifting snow.

properties.headline: High Wind Watch issued November 14 at 12:31PM AKST until November 17 at 6:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...West winds 50 to 65 mph with gusts up to 80 mph possible.

* WHERE...Shemya and Attu Islands.

* WHEN...From Monday evening through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...High winds could move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds rapidly increase in strength late Monday
evening and peak Tuesday morning as a strong low pressure system
moves through the Bering. Winds will gradually lighten through
Tuesday afternoon.
properties.instruction:
A high wind watch means there is potential for a hazardous high wind
event. Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates on this
situation. Fasten loose objects or shelter objects in a safe location
prior to the onset of winds.

properties.headline: Blizzard Warning issued November 14 at 9:54AM AKST until November 15 at 7:00AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions. Additional snow accumulations up to two
inches. Winds gusting as high as 60 mph.

* WHERE...Northern Arctic Coast.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM AKST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Snow and blowing snow could
reduce visibility below one half mile at times. Periods of blizzard
conditions will be intermittently possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The lull in snow and wind will continue
through Saturday morning before snowfall chances increase Saturday
afternoon through Sunday morning. Winds will increase thereafter
and be strongest Saturday afternoon into Sunday with gusts as high
as 60 mph possible and blizzard conditions returning.
properties.instruction:
Travel should be restricted to emergencies only. If you must travel,
have a winter survival kit with you. If you get stranded, stay with
your vehicle.
